newsitem.title: USA: CME traders call nearby CME cattle lower Monday.
newsitem.headline: CME traders call nearby CME cattle lower Monday.

text.p: CME livestock traders and analysts called USDA's Cattle-on-Feed report bearish for nearby CME cattle futures Monday, while the USDA cattle inventory report was slightly bullish for deferred contracts.

Traders expect August, October and possibly December live cattle to open about 0.25 cent per lb lower in reaction to the Cattle-on-Feed report showing July 1 cattle supplies at 117 percent of a year ago, slightly greater than the average of analysts' estimates.
Also, June marketings in the report were 102 percent of a year ago, which was less than the average estimate.

Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst at Alaron Trading Corp, said February and forward CME live cattle contracts may open higher Monday because the inventory report showed four-percent fewer heifers weighing 500 lbs or more will be going to feedlots this year.
Also, the report showed three percent fewer steers weighing 500 lbs will be headed to feedlots.
However, the report's total cattle and calf inventory number of 108.80 million head, or 98 percent of a year ago, was near the average of analysts' estimates, said Levitt.
